plan: candidate003 for module kda_swiglu_stage29_003: move the entire SwiGLU op into a C++ torch extension to cut the per-call Python/dispatcher overhead that candidate001's Triton path could not beat against vendor Torch's torch.compile fusion (native fwd 9.29us vs Triton 10.97us). Python is a thin boundary: validate metadata and raise NotImplementedError on CPU/FP32/odd-last-dim/noncontiguous inputs, then call the C++-exposed swiglu(x). The autograd graph node lives in C++ via torch::autograd::Function<Swiglu>: forward() saves the original contiguous x and launches one CUDA forward kernel; backward() reads saved x, canonicalizes grad_outputs[0] with .contiguous(), and launches one CUDA backward kernel, returning a single dx. This mirrors the native manual backward and removes Python autograd.Function engine callbacks. Arithmetic exactly reproduces the native contract in FP32 with only final stores rounded to BF16: gate=x[...,:H], up=x[...,H:], H=lastdim/2; a=gate,b=up,g=grad; sig=1/(1+exp(-a)); out=BF16(a*sig*b); dx_gate=BF16(g*sig*(1+a*(1-sig))*b); dx_up=BF16(g*(a*sig)). Indexing is flat: output element i -> row=i/H, col=i%H, gateidx=row*2H+col, upidx=gateidx+H; the backward kernel writes both gateidx and dx[upidx] from one thread, covering every element of dx once. Standard ATen CUDA APIs only: at::cuda::CUDAGuard(x.device()), at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream(), C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK(). BF16 handled via at::BFloat16* from data_ptr<at::BFloat16>() with static_cast<float>/at::BFloat16(value) conversions. No fast-math, no --fmad flag (candidate002 failure), no fp-contract pragma (controller builds with -O3 -ffp-contract=off), no vector/SM intrinsics, no RNG/timers/env reads/syncs/scans, no result caching. Loaded-module caching only. This is a hypothesis to reduce overhead below native Torch compiled fusion; it must pass all 22 numerical cases and the 3-seed/120-step/>1% gate before any promotion, with the default native bias_swiglu_impl staying enabled otherwise.
risks: 1) Overhead hypothesis may not hold: a hand-written C++ autograd Function plus two elementwise CUDA launches may still not beat vendor Torch's fused torch.compile SwiGLU (native 9.29us fwd / 81.79us fwd+bwd); only the controller's 3-seed measurement decides, and a positive mean with any regressing seed fails the gate. 2) BF16 rounding: at::BFloat16(float) rounding may differ bitwise from the native compiled path, but the contract only requires the fixed CPU-float64 atol 3e-4/rtol 1e-3 tolerance, not bit-exactness. 3) FP operation ordering depends on the controller's -ffp-contract=off; if contraction is re-enabled, a/dx ordering could drift from the probed native order. 4) at::BFloat16 device-side conversion operators must be available in CoreX clang-16 device code; prior CoreX extensions confirmed this, but it is version-sensitive. 5) The fixed .so path /tmp/kda-swiglu-stage29/cpp-build-003/kda_swiglu_stage29_003.so must match the controller's built artifact name; an ABI-suffixed filename would fail the importlib load. 6) Confidence of the underlying wiki kernel-fusion/gated-dual-gemm evidence is source-reported/experimental (NVIDIA SM100 fusion, CoreX Triton 2.1 probes) and does not establish BI-V150 production speedups; this remains unverified until measured.
